answer.generated: Concurrency control in a single-server architecture primarily manages concurrent access through local locking mechanisms, ensuring data integrity within the confines of a single machine. In contrast, a multi-server architecture introduces additional challenges and solutions, such as distributed locking and replication to handle concurrent transactions across multiple servers. Distribution requires coordination among servers to maintain consistency, while replication ensures data availability and fault tolerance. Parallelism further enhances performance by allowing concurrent execution of tasks across servers, but it necessitates sophisticated scheduling and coordination to manage the complexity of distributed transactions effectively.
